stem:
Potassium chloride, $\text{KCl}$, and magnesium chloride, $\text{MgCl}_2$, are both ionic solids.

Table 1.1

| energy change | value/$\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| standard enthalpy change of solution, $\Delta H^\ominus_{\text{sol}}$, of $\text{KCl}$ | +15 |
| lattice energy, $\Delta H^\ominus_{\text{latt}}$, of $\text{KCl(s)}$ | -701 |
| standard enthalpy change of hydration, $\Delta H^\ominus_{\text{hyd}}$, of $\text{K}^{+}$ | -322 |
| standard enthalpy change of hydration, $\Delta H^\ominus_{\text{hyd}}$, of $\text{Cl}^{-}$ | -364 |
| standard enthalpy change of solution, $\Delta H^\ominus_{\text{sol}}$, of $\text{MgCl}_2$ | -155 |
| lattice energy, $\Delta H^\ominus_{\text{latt}}$, of $\text{MgCl}_2\text{(s)}$ | -2493 |

parts.label: (a)
(b)
parts.text: Use the data in Table 1.1 to calculate the enthalpy change of hydration of magnesium ions, $\text{Mg}^{2+}$. Show your working.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain the reasons why the lattice energy of $\text{MgCl}_2$ is more exothermic than the lattice energy of $\text{KCl}$.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by entropy, $S$.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text:
Potassium chloride is very soluble in water at $20^\circ\text{C}$.

Explain the solubility of potassium chloride by reference to change in entropy, $\Delta S$.

parts.label: (e)(iii)
parts.text: Use the Gibbs equation and your answer to (e)(ii) to predict whether potassium chloride is more soluble in water at $20^\circ\text{C}$ or at $80^\circ\text{C}$. Explain your answer.
